trip_plan.totalNote: Three days: backpack to Fish Creek Pass, climb the Northwest Ridge as a long technical day from camp, and hike out.

days.title: Hike in to Fish Creek Pass
days.objective: Camp near Fish Creek Pass or at Star Lake
days.note: Backpack in on the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trail to a camp at Star Lake or near Fish Creek Pass.

days.title: Climb the Northwest Ridge
days.objective: Summit Star Peak via the ridge
days.note: Climb the ridge as a technical day trip from camp, allowing a full day for the approach and the ridge's sustained, low-angle length before the crux. The descent off the ridge is undocumented, so settle on a strategy (downclimb or rappel the ridge, or drop west to the Southwest Spur scramble) before committing above the…

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the West Fork Buttermilk Trailhead
days.note: Hike back out the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trail to the trailhead.

new_camps.name: Star Lake
new_camps.why: The usual base for Star Peak: water at the door, the ridge within reach for a full day, and a downhill carry out on day three.
new_camps.water: The lake and its outlet stream.
new_camps.capacity: Room for a few tents on the benches around the shore.
new_camps.permit: No limited-entry permit; keep tents 200 ft from the water.
new_camps.notes: About 7.5 miles and 3,500 ft from the West Fork Buttermilk trailhead; the upper trail is brushy, so the carry is slower than the mileage suggests. Camping just below Fish Creek Pass is the only other option parties mention.

days.title: Day 1
days.note: Ferry/floatplane to Stehekin, hike Company Creek Trail (~3 mi) to the leave-trail point.

days.title: Day 2
days.note: Traverse White Goat Mountain's west slopes and cross the ~7,200 ft pass above Bird Lakes to a high bivy in the Bird Lakes basin.

days.title: Day 3
days.note: Climb the East Face (class 2-4 with a 5.4-5.6 crux) to the summit and return to camp.

days.title: Day 4
days.note: Hike out to Stehekin.

new_camps.name: Company Creek Trail camp near the leave-trail point
new_camps.why: Day one is short after the boat, so parties stop near where the route leaves the trail and start the steep brush and slabs fresh the next morning.
new_camps.capacity: Informal; room for a small party.
new_camps.permit: Stehekin backcountry permit from the NPS.
new_camps.notes: Many parties instead cross to the Devore Creek trail and sleep at Bird Creek Camp, which cuts the next day's off-trail work; this plan's route goes over the Bird Lakes pass instead. Night one is the least documented of the trip.

new_camps.name: High bivy in the Bird Lakes basin
new_camps.why: Sleeping in the basin below the east face puts the climb a short walk away and keeps the summit day light; the last water is a trickle near the top larches.
new_camps.water: A small seep near the highest larches; carry water from the lakes.
new_camps.capacity: A few flat spots near the highest larch trees, about 200 ft above the creek.
new_camps.permit: Stehekin backcountry permit; bivy only, no fires.
new_camps.notes: Elevation is approximate. Reached after crossing the roughly 7,200 ft pass above Bird Lakes. Parties sleep here the night before and the night after the climb.

previous_research.plan_conflict: Plan sends parties over the Bird Lakes pass, but most reports reach Tupshin from Bird Creek Camp on the Devore Creek trail; night 1 is not confirmed.

name: South Ridge (via Asa Peak NE Ridge)

trip_plan.totalNote: A 5-day trip from High Bridge: PCT to a Swamp Creek camp, off-trail to Upper Blue Basin and a high camp near Icy-Spruce Pass, a very long summit day via the south ridge and chimney crux, and a long hike out.

days.title: High Bridge to Swamp Creek camp
days.objective: Reach a camp in the Swamp Creek area
days.note: Hike the PCT from High Bridge about 8.5 miles to a camp in the Swamp Creek area, roughly 5.2 hours.

days.title: Climb to Upper Blue Basin
days.objective: Reach camp in Upper Blue Basin
days.note: Cross Agnes Creek and Spruce Creek on logs, then climb steeply off-trail through brush, talus and slabs to a camp in Upper Blue Basin at about 5,000 ft.

days.title: Move to Icy-Spruce Pass high camp
days.objective: Reach a high camp near Icy-Spruce Pass
days.note: Move camp up to a high camp near Icy-Spruce Pass at about 6,760 ft.

days.title: Summit via the south ridge
days.objective: Summit via the south ridge and chimney crux
days.note: Make the summit push via the south ridge and its chimney crux, about 8.5 hours up and 7 hours back to high camp for a typical party (a slower party took 10.6 up and 8.8 down). Return to high camp.

days.title: Hike out to High Bridge
days.objective: Return to High Bridge
days.note: Break camp and hike out to High Bridge.

new_camps.name: Swamp Creek area camp on the PCT
new_camps.why: The end of an easy 8.5 miles on the PCT and the last good water and flat ground before the steep off-trail climb the next morning.
new_camps.capacity: Several sites near the creek crossing.
new_camps.notes: Also the usual first camp for Needle Peak and Lyall. Logs across Agnes and Spruce Creeks start day two.

new_camps.name: Upper Blue Basin camp
new_camps.why: The first flat ground after a brutal brush, talus and slab climb; stopping here splits the carry before the final move to the pass.
new_camps.water: Snowmelt and small streams in the basin.
new_camps.notes: Off-trail, no maintained path; expect a slow day two. Reports of this basin are thin.

new_camps.name: High camp near Icy-Spruce Pass
new_camps.why: The high camp for the south ridge: it makes the 8-9 hour summit push possible from camp and is the base you return to before hiking out.
new_camps.water: Snow patches or a nearby tarn; check in late season.
new_camps.notes: Reached after about 1,760 ft of steep ground above Upper Blue Basin. Parties camp on the divide or on the col below the peak.

trip_plan.totalNote: Hike and climb the technical approach to the bivy caves, climb all 14 pitches the next day, then walk off to the Barclay Lake trailhead.

days.title: Approach to the Dolomite Tower bivy caves
days.objective: Reach the bivy caves below the tower
days.note: Hike in and complete the 3-3.5 hour technical approach, a forested rib with fixed lines and a roped slab, to the bivy caves below the tower.

days.title: Climb Vanishing Point
days.objective: Climb all 14 pitches
days.note: Climb the full 14-pitch route, a very long day given the sustained 5.10-5.12 climbing with few easy pitches.

days.title: Walk off to the trailhead
days.objective: Return to the Barclay Lake trailhead
days.note: Descend via the roughly 3-hour descent route back to the trailhead, or do this the same day if fast.

camps_on_file.name: Dolomite Tower bivy caves
camps_on_file.notes: Shallow caves about 150 ft right of the start of the route. Spray can blow in during wind and rain.

camps.name: Dolomite Tower bivy caves
camps.why: Three flat platforms in shallow caves right of the start, one person each, so the 14 pitches begin from the base; spray blows in during wind and rain.

previous_research.plan_conflict: Recent parties often do the approach, climb and descent car-to-car in one long day (about 12.5 hours), using the caves only when slower or splitting the trip.

trip_plan.totalNote: Historically this was a multi-year siege climb with fixed ropes and multiple camps; the modern standard plan is a 2-day round trip with one bivy atop the crux step — roughly 7 hours of approach/lower climbing plus 8 hours to finish and descend (15 hours of combined movement). Very strong, fast parties have compressed the whole route into a single long day car-to-car (documented in a 2013 trip report), but this requires exceptional fitness, dry/stable conditions, and prior route knowledge; most parties should plan for 2 days minimum given the loose rock and difficult retreat.

days.title: Approach and climb the lower two steps to a high bivy
days.objective: Hike in from Barclay Lake Trailhead, climb Steps 1 and 2 (including the crux), and bivy atop the crux step
days.note: From the Barclay Lake Trailhead, follow the old logging road to the climbers'-trail cairn, then the boot path and creek bed upstream through steep brush, forest, and loose dirt to Couloir Camp (~4,300 ft). Continue between the two parallel rock ribs flanking the summit couloir to the base of the wall, then climb Step 1…

days.title: Finish the face and descend the south side
days.objective: Climb Steps 3 and 4 to the summit, then descend the non-technical walk-off
days.note: From the high bivy, climb Step 3 (220 ft, Grade V) and Step 4 (250 ft, Grade V, the final vertical step) to the summit ridge, then finish easier terrain to Baring's true summit. Descend the non-technical south-side walk-off back to the Barclay Lake Trailhead, carrying a rope and rack in case a rappel is needed if you f…

camps_on_file.name: Couloir Camp
Barclay Lake
camps_on_file.notes: This is the one genuinely established camp in the zone and the obvious base for the Barclay Creek peaks. It sits at 2,420 ft in a narrow trench with Baring Mountain's north face rising straight out of the south shore and Merchant Peak and Gunn Peak on the north side, so nearly every objective on that road starts from h…

camps_on_file.name: Dolomite Camp
camps_on_file.notes: Camp at the base of the first of the four vertical steps, after the brush-fighting approach.

camps.name: Dolomite Camp
camps.why: Perched above the first step, it is the camp parties haul to and sleep at on the face, with a snow patch for water and a short push to the upper steps.

camps.name: Couloir Camp
camps.why: A forested staging ledge about 1,000 ft above the lake; most parties pass through it to Dolomite Camp, using it only to split loads or sit out a bad day.

camps.name: Barclay Lake
camps.why: Comfortable lakeside sites at the trailhead end of the approach; it adds a long brush-bash to day one, so it suits only a slow party or a retreat.

previous_research.plan_conflict: The plan puts the bivy atop the crux step, but the only documented camp on the face is Dolomite Camp at the top of the first step; Couloir Camp and Barclay Lake were both marked main and are now route (they are not slept at on a two-day plan).

name: Infinite Beauty

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip: backpack about 12 miles to the Waptus River bridge, climb the Mega Slab and 5.6+ summit block, then hike out.

days.title: Backpack to the Waptus River bridge
days.objective: Camp near the Waptus River PCT bridge
days.note: Backpack in on the Waptus River Trail and the PCT to a camp near the Waptus River bridge, about 12 miles.

days.title: Climb Infinite Beauty
days.objective: Climb the Mega Slab and summit block
days.note: Hike to the lowest point of the Mega Slab, climb the shallow-rib start and merge with Timeless Treasure's line, then finish with 3 pitches of 5.6+ on the summit block. Descend via Shovel Lake or the ascent line.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Salmon La Sac trailhead
days.note: Pack up and hike out to the trailhead.

refused_because: new camp "Camp near the Waptus River PCT bridge" has no researched elevation; night 2 has 0 main camps

new_camps.name: Camp near the Waptus River PCT bridge
new_camps.why: About an hour from the slab base along the old Shovel Creek track, which makes this the standard camp for the Mega Slab climbs.
new_camps.notes: One party camped at an abandoned trail near Shovel Creek instead, and carried river shoes for the Waptus crossing. Elevation was not found in any source.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip: hike about 15 miles up the Middle Fork Snoqualmie to Dutch Miller Gap and a camp below the face, climb the SW Face, then hike out.

days.title: Hike to Dutch Miller Gap
days.objective: Camp below the SW Face
days.note: Hike about 15 miles up the Middle Fork Snoqualmie on the Dutch Miller Gap Trail to Dutch Miller Gap, then continue to a camp below the SW Face.

days.title: Climb the SW Face
days.objective: Summit via the SW Face and return to camp
days.note: Climb about 1,000 ft of gully scrambling and then the 3-pitch summit block, roughly 6 hours from camp to summit. Descend by rappels and downclimbing back to camp, a little under 5 hours.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the trailhead
days.note: Hike back out to the trailhead.

new_camps.name: Dutch Miller Gap camp
new_camps.why: The standard night after a long 15-mile walk-in, with established sites and ponds at the gap, leaving a six-hour summit day with a night's rest.
new_camps.permit: Free self-issue wilderness permit at the trailhead.
new_camps.notes: Gap elevation is about 5,000 ft; sites sit at or just below it.

new_camps.name: Tarns below the Southwest Face, about 5,300 ft
new_camps.why: Moving up from the gap shortens the summit morning, at the cost of carrying packs another uphill mile past the gap.
new_camps.notes: Used by a 2020 party who moved camp from the gap the same evening.

name: Timeless Treasure

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip: backpack about 12 miles to the Waptus River bridge, climb ~3,000 ft of 4th-class slab and the 5.6+ summit block, then hike out.

days.title: Climb Timeless Treasure

trip_plan.totalNote: A three-day plan: hike from Pete Lake Trailhead to the big-boulder bivy below the Chimney Glacier, spend a long day on the 9-10 pitch East Face Direct with many rappels, and hike out (fit parties compress this to two days with a headlamp walk-out).

Leave the PCT at the second switchback and head northwest to cross the North Fork of Lemah Creek at about 3,380 ft. Then follow the flagged boot path steeply to the big boulder bivy at about 4,600-4,8…

days.title: Hike out to Pete Lake Trailhead
days.objective: Return to the trailhead
days.note: Descend the boot path to the creek crossing, rejoin the PCT, and walk the long, flat trail past Pete Lake to the car; one party took about 3.5 hours from the bivy.

camps.name: Pete Lake and the Lemah Meadows camps

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip using the same Pete Lake approach and high camp as the East Face. The summit day climbs wet fourth-class ground and ledges left of the main gully to the notch between the central and south summits, then continues to the South Peak (7,440 ft), descending the same way with single-rope rappels - roughly 18.5 miles round trip.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip for most parties: hike in to a high camp below the Chimney Glacier, a long summit day climbing 3 pitches of low-5th-class rock on the East Face with a multi-rappel descent, then hike out — roughly 19 miles and 6,000 ft round trip.

days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach the bivy camp below Chimney Glacier
days.note: From the Pete Lake trailhead, hike to Pete Lake, join the PCT, then drop off-trail near the Lemah Creek drainage and follow a climber's boot path up steep, brushy slopes to a bivy camp (Sunrise Knob / the 4,650-4,800 ft boulder camp) below the toe of the Chimney Glacier.

days.title: Summit day: Chimney Glacier and the East Face
days.objective: Climb the East Face and reach the summit
days.note: An alpine start up the moraine and glacier to the base of the face, then 3 pitches of wet, slippery low-5th-class rock (running belays on the easier ground) to the notch and summit blocks. Descent reverses the face via a series of rappels back to the glacier, often finishing at camp in twilight.

camps.why: A lower option at the road end; it spares the cross-country day with a heavy pack but adds miles and gain to summit day.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day loop: hike past Deception Pass and Marmot Lake to camp at Jade Lake, then cross Dip Top Gap to Pea Soup Lake, climb the Lynch Glacier to the summit, and descend the Hyas side via Peggy's Pond to the trailhead.

days.title: Hike in to Jade Lake
days.objective: Camp at Jade Lake (~5,500 ft)
days.note: Deception Pass trail from Tucquala Meadows (~3,400 ft) to Marmot Lake, then the rough path past No-Name Lake to Jade Lake, about 9.7 miles and 3,200 ft. Alternatively camp at the Pea Soup Lake outlet over Dip Top Gap to shorten summit day.

days.title: Lynch Glacier to the summit and out
days.objective: Summit Mount Daniel and return to the trailhead
days.note: Climb the snow couloir to Dip Top Gap (steep, exposed snow and loose scree), traverse down to the Pea Soup Lake outlet, then take the snow finger (or a Class 3 bypass late season) and the Lynch Glacier to the col between the middle and true summits. Descend southeast via the Hyas Glacier snowfield to Peggy's Pond and o…

camps_on_file.name: Peggy's Pond, below Cathedral Rock
camps_on_file.notes: The base for Mount Daniel and the eastern option for Mount Hinman, and by a distance the most convenient high camp on this side of the divide. Drive the Cle Elum River road north from Salmon la Sac roughly eleven to twelve miles of rough, narrow gravel to the Tucquala Meadows trailhead at the road end, take the Cathedr…

camps_on_file.name: Hyas Lake and Upper Hyas Lake
camps_on_file.notes: The low-effort basecamp on the Cle Elum side, less than two miles up the Deception Pass trail from the Tucquala Meadows road end on a gentle grade through meadow and forest, sitting at about 3,471 ft with Cathedral Rock and the Daniel massif standing over it. For Mount Daniel it is the family-friendly alternative to Pe…

camps.name: Peggy's Pond, below Cathedral Rock
camps.why: The pond is where this loop ends, not where it sleeps: you pass it on summit day on the way down to the trailhead.

camps.name: Hyas Lake and Upper Hyas Lake
camps.why: An easy low camp close to the trailhead for a three-day trip; it adds a long climb to Deception Pass and the lakes before the glacier.

previous_research.plan_conflict: Night 1 is at Jade Lake (or Pea Soup Lake outlet) in this plan, and neither is on file; I found no verified elevation for either, so no main camp is listed for night 1.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day backpack for most parties: roughly 23 miles round trip and ~6,000 ft of cumulative gain, basing at La Bohn Lakes/Jade Lake and making a long class 2-3 scramble summit day (the historic Hinman Glacier has largely melted out); very fit parties occasionally push it car-to-car in ~15 hours, but that is not the standard/recommended plan.

days.title: Backpack in to La Bohn Lakes / Jade Lake
days.objective: Establish high camp near La Bohn Gap
days.note: Hike the East Fork Foss / Necklace Valley Trail (steep and rooty in spots, with swampy, mosquito-prone lake basins) up into Necklace Valley and toward La Bohn Gap, camping at La Bohn Lakes or Jade Lake — the standard base camp used by nearly all parties climbing Hinman.

days.title: Summit day: La Bohn Gap to Mount Hinman
days.objective: Reach the summit of Mount Hinman (7,492 ft) and return to camp
days.note: Climb through La Bohn Gap and follow broad class 2-3 ridge/scramble terrain to the summit; the historic Hinman Glacier has largely melted out, so expect rock and receding snow patches rather than true glacier travel on most late-summer ascents. Reverse the route back to camp.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Necklace Valley trailhead
days.note: Retrace the Necklace Valley Trail back down through the valley and along the East Fork Foss River to the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: La Bohn Lakes, La Bohn Gap and the Chain Lakes benches
camps_on_file.notes: The high camp for La Bohn Peak and the launching point for the west route on Mount Hinman, and the single most useful piece of ground in this zone for a climber. La Bohn Gap is a broad boulder-covered saddle at roughly 6,000 ft on the crest between the Foss and Snoqualmie drainages, with the tarns of the La Bohn Lakes …

camps_on_file.name: Necklace Valley — Jade, Emerald and Opal Lakes
camps_on_file.notes: The main basecamp for La Bohn Peak, which stands directly at the head of this valley, and the first night of the standard west-side approach to Mount Hinman. Drive the Foss River road off Highway 2 a short way east of Skykomish and turn into the Necklace Valley trailhead about four miles up. The trail is famously two-f…

camps_on_file.name: Money Creek and Miller River campgrounds, Foss River roadhead
camps_on_file.notes: The valley-bottom staging option for every Foss River objective, and worth a line of its own because of what the road has been doing. The Foss River road leaves Highway 2 just east of Skykomish and has been running weekday construction delays of about half an hour through the summer, with damage further up that has at …

camps.name: La Bohn Lakes, La Bohn Gap and the Chain Lakes benches
camps.why: Camps right under the gap, so summit day is a short scramble; the price is a longer, steeper first day with a snow slope to the gap.

camps.name: Necklace Valley — Jade, Emerald and Opal Lakes
camps.why: Established lake sites about eight to nine miles in, lower and buggier; stopping here keeps day one easier but adds the gap climb to summit day.

camps.name: Money Creek and Miller River campgrounds, Foss River roadhead
camps.why: Car campgrounds for the night before an early trailhead start; useful for a Friday-night arrival, though the Foss River road has had delays.

previous_research.plan_conflict: Both La Bohn Lakes and Necklace Valley are on file as main; only one can be main for night 1, so Necklace Valley is changed to route.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip: hike up the East Fork Foss into Necklace Valley and camp at the lakes, climb over La Bohn Gap to La Bohn Lakes and up the broad ridge to Hinman, then hike out.

days.title: Hike in to Necklace Valley
days.objective: Camp at the Necklace Valley lakes
days.note: The first 5 miles are gentle forest gaining about 600 ft to the East Fork Foss footlog, then about 2,400 ft in three miles of steep, rooty trail to Jade Lake and on to Emerald Lake; roughly 9 miles and 3,400 ft. Established sites at Jade Lake; Emerald and Opal lakes are quieter.

days.title: Climb Hinman via La Bohn Gap
days.objective: Summit Mount Hinman and return to camp
days.note: From the head of the valley go off-trail to La Bohn Gap (the waterfall line is usually preferred over the gully), past La Bohn Lakes, then up the broad, mostly Class 2 ridge, crossing the upper remnants of the north-side glaciers to the summit ridge. The true high point is ambiguous and many parties stop at a near-equa…

days.title: Hike out the East Fork Foss
days.objective: Return to the trailhead
days.note: Reverse the steep descent from Jade Lake to the river crossing, then the flat forest walk out.

new_camps.name: Necklace Valley — Jade, Emerald and Opal Lakes
new_camps.why: Established lake sites at the end of the nine-mile first day; Emerald and Opal give quieter sites and a shorter push to the gap.
new_camps.permit: A wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead at no fee.
new_camps.notes: Jade Lake has established sites and gets buggy early. Campfires are not allowed.

trip_plan.totalNote: A remote 3-day/2-night trip: ~40 miles round trip and ~6,000 ft net gain, with the crux being the exposed 4th-class summit block and a steep snow finger above the Overcoat Glacier; a few very fit parties have done it car-to-car in ~15 hrs during good spring ski-mountaineering conditions, but that is a fast-party exception, not the standard plan.

days.title: Bike/hike approach to Overcoat Glacier Camp
days.objective: Reach high camp on rock benches above the Overcoat Glacier (~6,600 ft)
days.note: Bike the old roadbed and Dutch Miller Gap Trail corridor from Dingford Creek, ford the Middle Fork Snoqualmie, then push up through brush, talus and the 'Valley of the Chiefs' benches to camp near Overcoat Lake/glacier. It's a long, grinding approach day with little technical difficulty but a lot of vertical and bushwh…

days.title: Summit push and camp relocation
days.objective: Climb the east-face ledges and gully to the summit, then move camp toward the exit
days.note: Cross the glacier and climb steep snow to the base of the summit rock, then finish on exposed 4th-class ledges and a gully to the 7,432 ft summit; reverse via two rappels back to the glacier. Rather than return to the same camp, most parties then break camp and hike out toward Bears Breast Tarns the same afternoon to s…

days.title: Exit to trailhead
days.objective: Hike and bike back to the Dingford Creek Trailhead
days.note: An optional short side trip to Williams Lake, then a straightforward but long hike back down the Middle Fork corridor to the horse camp, followed by a quick downhill bike ride to the car.

camps_on_file.name: Overcoat Lake
Rock benches above Overcoat Glacier
Hardscrabble Horse Camp, Middle Fork Snoqualmie
camps_on_file.notes: The staging camp for the whole Middle Fork half of this zone, and the answer to the question of what to do with a seven-mile road walk. Forest Road 56 is rough — potholes, ruts and washed river-rock sections that want high clearance — and it is gated at Dingford Creek, so the last roughly seven miles to the horse camp …

camps.name: Rock benches above Overcoat Glacier
camps.why: The highest camp, at the base of the summit snow; it makes summit day short but means a hard, brushy carry up from the valley.

camps.name: Overcoat Lake
camps.why: A lower base reached after the same brush, with water; it saves some of the carry but adds climbing to summit day.

camps.name: Hardscrabble Horse Camp, Middle Fork Snoqualmie
camps.why: The end of the bike ride and the last night before the car; it keeps the loaded carry short but makes day one a long ride and walk.

previous_research.plan_conflict: Night 2 is spent near Bears Breast Tarns per the plan, which is not on file, and I could not confirm its elevation, so night 2 has no main camp; Overcoat Lake and the benches are both on file as main for night 1, so Overcoat Lake is changed to route.

trip_plan.totalNote: Two days: approach up the Middle Fork Snoqualmie valley to camp below the north face, then climb the ~2,000 ft ice line, descend and hike out.

days.title: Approach to camp below the north face
days.objective: Establish camp below the north face
days.note: Bike or hike into the Middle Fork Snoqualmie valley, then continue on foot along the valley trail, fording the braids of the Middle Fork Snoqualmie River. Establish camp below the north face; the first-ascent party took about 6.5 hours from the vehicle.

days.title: Climb the north face and hike out
days.objective: Climb the ice line and return to the car
days.note: Make an alpine start around 6 AM and climb the roughly 2,000 ft ice line. Descend the southwest-side gully with two 30 m rappels and hike back out.

previous_research.plan_conflict: Parties camp on the valley floor of the Middle Fork Snoqualmie close under the face, but no source gave an elevation, so no camp entry could be added for night 1.
